def peekn(n, seq):
    """ Retrieve the first n elements of a sequence

    Returns a tuple of (items, rest) where items is a list of the first n
    elements and rest is an iterable containing those same elements followed
    by the remaining elements of the original sequence.

    >>> seq = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    >>> items, rest = peekn(2, seq)
    >>> items
    [0, 1]
    >>> list(rest)
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]

    If the sequence has fewer than n elements, all elements are returned:

    >>> items, rest = peekn(5, [1, 2])
    >>> items
    [1, 2]
    >>> list(rest)
    [1, 2]

    See Also:
        peek
    """
    iterator = iter(seq)
    items = []
    for _ in range(n):
        try:
            item = next(iterator)
            items.append(item)
        except StopIteration:
            break
    return items, itertools.chain(items, iterator)
